error_acknowledgment: The original plan incorrectly identified GPIO_BC@0x28 as the final GD32F4xx GPIO register and exclusive end0x2c. I stopped the original lookup at line62 and omitted the following GPIO_TG definition. That underbounded plan must not be used for the new read output-overlap guard.

corrected_fact.header_macro: #define GPIO_TG(gpiox)             REG32((gpiox) + 0x2CU)    /*!< GPIO port bit toggle register */
corrected_fact.bc_macro: #define GPIO_BC(gpiox)             REG32((gpiox) + 0x28U)    /*!< GPIO bit clear register */
corrected_fact.replacement_scope: Replace every original plan occurrence of last-register BC / extent0x2c / size44 with last-register TG / extent0x30 / size48. BC remains included. Applies to GD470 only; F407 still uses actual sizeof(GPIO_TypeDef).

SDK_applicability.byte_checks: Independently checked full actual size/SHA of gd32f4xx_gpio.h, gd32f4xx_gpio.c and gd32f4xx.h against the maintained source.lock.json; each also matches current Main index blob.
SDK_applicability.variant: The common gd32f4xx.h explicitly accepts GD32F470; current Nexus SoC is exact GD32F470ZGT6. GPIO_TG is unconditional in this locked shared GPIO register definitions block, with GPIOA-I bases. No narrower chip conditional surrounds it.
SDK_applicability.vendor_implementation: The same locked official source defines gpio_bit_toggle and gpio_port_toggle, both directly writing GPIO_TG(gpio_periph); their comments list GPIOA-I. Thus TG is a command-register interface in the exact SDK used by the current F470 provider, not a guessed register from another series.
SDK_applicability.scope_limit: This establishes the source/API span applicable to the selected GD32F470 build. It does not independently qualify every F4 member, physical silicon revision, timing or electrical toggle behavior.

reference_manual_boundary.repository_reference: soc/gd32f470/README.md records GD32F470xx Datasheet Rev2.2 and GD32F4xx User Manual Rev3.3 as maintained source references for this exact provider.
reference_manual_boundary.actual_review_today: The original PDF/raw extracted GPIO register chapter was not present in this bounded input set and was not downloaded/reopened. Therefore no fresh RM page/paragraph statement about TG is claimed. The actual independent evidence here is the fully hash-locked official SDK definitions and implementation plus exact F470 target selection.
reference_manual_boundary.why_no_blocker_to_this_fix: The correction only prevents writing read output into the complete owned GPIO bank. It does not add TG access to any production GPIO operation. Even a revision-specific reserved word must not be treated as ordinary caller output RAM; conservative denial does not assert new hardware capability.

implementation_delta.gd_guard: Use the correct exclusive end0x30 / official GPIO_TG plus sizeof(uint32_t) when deriving the owned bank interval. Preserve safe integer range checks and existing mask/liveness/context semantics. No register probing, new state, API, policy, GPIO write or Board route added.
implementation_delta.tests_first: Both GPIO_BC and GPIO_TG must be distinct real aligned-MMIO output-alias regression probes in the existing GD whole Google program. Keep original mask/state and all other registers byte-identical after INVALID, and preserve every old test assertion.
implementation_delta.RED_meaning: The baseline unguarded production read writes masked input to either alias and returns SUCCESS; this is a predicted substantive failure until author actually executes tests-only RED. A too-short BC-only guard would also incorrectly admit TG. Use mapped register bytes/sentinels to observe the bad store, not a mocked provider.
implementation_delta.observation_limit: Native mapped TG value changes prove an unintended MMIO command-register store; do not label that as measured physical pin toggle. This researcher did not execute either new case.
implementation_delta.interval_boundary: TG word [base+0x2c,base+0x30) is protected. The exclusive end arithmetic is not permission to use another/reserved MMIO word at base+0x30 as valid output storage. Valid-instance isolation and ordinary RAM output tests remain required.

qualification: IO31 remains pending/not_qualified/not_executed. This is only the agreed ownership prerequisite. No Board wiring, sleep-state transition, wake retention, HIL or whole-series qualification changes.
